title: Synergy of strength–ductility in HfMoTaTiZr refractory high entropy alloy through Cr addition

recollection.starting_material: The base alloy was a refractory high-entropy alloy consisting of Hf, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr.
recollection.intervention: Cr was added to the base composition, likely via melting and homogenization techniques, to modify the alloy’s microstructure and properties.
recollection.structure: The addition of Cr is presumed to induce a dual-phase or multiphase microstructure. Likely, a primary BCC phase was retained while a secondary phase (perhaps Cr-rich precipitates or an ordered phase) formed, providing a synergy between strength and ductility.
recollection.mechanism: The improved mechanical behavior is guessed to stem from a combination of solid-solution strengthening and precipitation (or phase boundary) strengthening. The Cr addition likely promotes controlled precipitation/nanostructuring that retards dislocation motion, thereby enhancing strength, while also activating additional deformation mechanisms that boost ductility.
recollection.results: Quantitatively, the alloy might exhibit a significant increase in yield strength—possibly in the range of 20-30% improvement—while maintaining or even enhancing ductility (for example, elongation values reaching 10-15%). These numbers are speculative but illustrate the typical target improvements when balancing strength and ductility in refractory high-entropy alloys.

score.note: Correctly identifies Cr addition, retention of a BCC matrix with a secondary phase, and broadly plausible solid-solution/second-phase strengthening. However, it omits the specific 4.2 at.% Cr addition, reticulated Cr₂(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase, crack-hindrance/plasticity-compensation mechanism, and measured values. The speculative 10–15% ductility range includes the actual 14.0%, but no close yield-strength, phase-fraction, or hardness values are recalled.
